bug_semantics: A plugin executing without PluginCapability.READ_FILES was supposed to be confined to the sandbox temporary directory and explicitly safe paths. The sandbox enforced that policy only by replacing builtins.open with restricted_open. Plugin code could instead import pathlib or io and call pathlib.Path.read_text/read_bytes/write_text/write_bytes/open or io.open; those independent entry points never reached restricted_open, so the plugin could read or modify arbitrary host files, for example Path('/etc/passwd').read_text(), despite lacking the file capability. The repository advisory specifically describes the bypass in threading mode and notes that process isolation had a separate broader restriction failure.
flaw_origin: Commit 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef is the smallest public first-writer: it creates plugin_sandbox.py and the plugin subsystem, advertises file-system capability enforcement, but _restrict_file_operations patches only builtins.open. Its single parent 649f737a9f04645508d079c0c772a8a2b4c7457a has no plugin_sandbox.py at the affected path. Later commits 642fb2bdec8af6f1d592c322dfa98647e145fcef, 35499f201ae2dc531d1194f6810c953d8b9af78b, and ccb60e1a29ef67700128ca54eb25a95413d71ff1 revise restoration, allowed-path context, and AST validation while retaining the builtins-only restriction, so they are carriers/hardening changes rather than introducers.
ai_marker: The BIC commit object has human author and committer Tobi <tobster@brain-force.ch>, and its message contains the exact AI provenance lines '🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)' and 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>'. These are on the BIC itself, not inferred from a PR, branch, tag, later refactor, or fix.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security/advisories/GHSA-mcjj-qw7m-j3cp names the pathlib.Path/io.open bypass, gives the Path('/etc/passwd').read_text() PoC, states affected versions <1.4.0, and identifies d0be3e9 as its fix on releases/1.4.x. In the validated clone, `git log --all --reverse -S'restricted_open' -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` starts with 8a5ed7e6, followed only by later refactoring and the d0be3e9 fix. `git log -L 479,506:openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py d0be3e989b1632eadb68e17d07294cbf9ac57c1f^` traces the vulnerable function back to 8a5ed7e6 and shows its initial `builtins.open = restricted_open`; the intervening 642fb2bd, 35499f20, and ccb60e1a edits preserve that design. `git show --format=fuller 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` shows the file created from /dev/null and the builtins-only implementation. `git show -s --format='%H%n%P%n%an <%ae>%n%cn <%ce>%n%B' 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef` gives the sole parent, author/committer, and exact Claude markers. `git ls-tree -r --name-only 649f737a9f04645508d079c0c772a8a2b4c7457a -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` prints nothing, directly verifying parent absence. `git show --format=fuller d0be3e989b1632eadb68e17d07294cbf9ac57c1f` shows the direct fix saving, patching, and restoring io.open plus pathlib.Path.open/read/write/unlink/mkdir/rmdir methods so they enforce _is_safe_path. Its immediate parent e0c999ea44429e8de00b4acb3ba570efdc733092 had already added pathlib/io to shared AST/import blocklists, but d0be3e9 completes the fix for references bound before sandbox execution and is the repository advisory's named direct fix. `git tag --contains 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef --sort=version:refname` starts at v1.3.0 and includes v1.3.0-v1.3.6; `git tag --contains d0be3e989b1632eadb68e17d07294cbf9ac57c1f --sort=version:refname` starts at v1.4.0. `git diff --stat v1.2.1..v1.3.0 -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` shows the sandbox file absent from v1.2.1 and present in v1.3.0, while `git diff v1.3.6..v1.4.0 -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` shows the builtins-only implementation replaced by the io/pathlib coverage. Thus released v1.3.0 through v1.3.6 are affected and v1.4.0 is the first tagged fixed release.
reasoning: The security boundary and its flawed implementation arrive together in the BIC: there was no earlier plugin sandbox for a human change merely to expose, move, or activate. The BIC explicitly promises capability-based file restrictions yet implements only one Python file-opening surface, leaving commonplace equivalent APIs unrestricted. The direct parent lacks the entire affected file, and line/pickaxe history rejects later refactors as first-writers. The BIC commit object itself explicitly attributes generation and co-authorship to Claude. Because AI-authored code created both the new attack surface and the root protection-mechanism failure, rather than merely carrying an old defect or contributing a later flawed change, the appropriate closed verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
